decision: Accept the verified evaluation environments and descriptive baseline. No public learner, controller, error-envelope or universal-system qualification is promoted.
diagnosis: Selected Crazyflow artifact has exactly zero nonlinear output and hidden-memory readout weights; its remaining forecast is affine in observations and commands, using only the explicit 100 ms history despite a 500 ms public context requirement. Identical additive command perturbations therefore have history-independent predicted responses. This is a demonstrated limitation and a plausible contributor to world-velocity response error, not a causal ablation proving the sole cause.

independent_numpy_audit.score_scope: all 250 ms endpoint groups; other horizons and whole-prefix metrics verified by production replay
independent_numpy_audit.script_uses: stdlib and NumPy; no Glassbox reducer import

limits: Two fixed simulator configurations; no real-aircraft, arbitrary-system or controller qualification.
Crazyflow has 44 altitude-invalid parents; errors use valid truth prefixes with every planned missing slot retained. No complete-cohort primary Crazyflow RMSE claim.
Primary and each shift family remain separate; stronger maneuvers expose forecast and coverage losses.
Structured and generic share recording pool/roles but have different priors, windows, histories, observed-position availability, objectives and compute; no equal-compute architecture conclusion.
Current Cascade physics differs from Dart historical comparison; its old turn failure is not retrospectively fixed by this broader baseline.
Paired responses are finite interventions, not derivative qualification. Wind is unobserved by both predictors.
Saved mean/prediction/physics replay is exact; optimizer trajectories are not refitted as an independent qualification.
